$comment: P2-19: experimental crosswalk from AMC Layer 0 controls to the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026. Entries use the P1-09 crosswalk format plus support. AI-drafted; not reviewed. It stays experimental until a named expert signs it off (P1-34). A crosswalk entry never satisfies a target, an obligation or a control.
title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
source: ASI01 to ASI10 as listed in docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md and catalog/vocabulary.yaml; titles to re-verify against the primary source before publishing

reused.$comment: P1-48's scenario-to-ASI mapping, used as is and not restated here: each adversarial case's owaspAsi tags and the L0-ADV controls' own crosswalk entries.

entries.rationale: A signed tool allowlist refuses tools outside it; misuse of an allowed tool within its arguments is not covered by this control alone.
Limits on amount, recipient, resource and rate enforced outside the model bound how far an allowed tool can be misused.
Attributing every tool call to a unique agent bound to a human principal makes privilege use traceable; it does not by itself prevent abuse.
Short-lived, scoped, signed leases narrow the privileges an agent identity can exercise and refuse expired or revoked ones.
Delegation that never widens scope, limits or expiry addresses privilege escalation through subagents.
Pinning model, prompt, tool and corpus versions in a signed manifest refuses an unpinned or changed component.
An AI bill of materials with component digests records the agentic supply chain; it detects but does not block a compromised component.
Remote MCP servers used only with authorization limits untrusted tool servers entering the supply chain.
A kill switch with a manual fallback stops new protected effects, bounding a cascade once detected.
Stopping new effects or entering a recorded safe state on a provider outage keeps one failure from propagating into effects.
An approval bound to the exact action digest prevents an agent from obtaining consent for one action and performing another.
Override and rubber-stamp telemetry surfaces reviewers who approve without scrutiny, a symptom of misplaced trust in the agent.
Disclosing that the agent is an AI at first interaction addresses one form of human trust exploitation.
An operator kill switch can stop a rogue agent's new protected effects; it does not detect the agent going rogue.
Revoking an agent credential stops new protected actions within the profile's time bound.
A signed registry entry for every running agent makes an unregistered agent visible as such.

gaps.reason: No Layer 0 control states execution containment. The native-shell sandbox (P0-06, P1-05) is an enforcement point in docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md, not a catalog control, so no control maps to Unexpected Code Execution yet.

No Layer 0 control covers the integrity or authentication of messages between agents. L0-IDN-03 bounds delegated authority but not the channel; the threat model lists only in-process ACP session binding (P2-25).
